title: US company’s AI lets Ukraine’s cheap kamikaze drones track targets on their own
excerpt: $100 million deal gives 50,000 Ukrainian drones US-developed AI capabilities.
content_html:
It’s swarmin’ time

$100 million deal gives 50,000 Ukrainian drones US-developed AI capabilities.

Drones equipped with Auterion's Nemyx swarm autonomy system crash into a self-propelled gun during a test demonstration. Credit: Lorenz Meier | Auterion

Ukrainian drone operators have destroyed many Russian armored vehicles on the ground and even military helicopters in midair using $400 Shrike drones with explosive payloads. Now thousands of such drones are getting upgraded with an AI system capable of autonomously tracking and homing in on moving targets.

In mid-July, the Ukrainian military began receiving Shrike drones made by the Ukrainian company SkyFall equipped with AI-powered autonomy hardware and software developed by the US company Auterion. The companies plan to deliver 50,000 drones equipped with Auterion’s Skynode S strike kits in the coming months.

That allows human operators to manually fly the Shrike first-person view (FPV) drones into a battlefield area, designate a target up to half a mile away, and then “flip the switch to turn it into fire-and-forget terminal guidance mode,” Lorenz Meier, co-founder and CEO of Auterion, told Ars.

The operator can abort a strike or choose a different target as long as they have a radio signal connection with the drone, Meier explained. But the drone can still automatically track and fly into targets without any human guidance, even if it loses its connection with the operator due to buildings or terrain blocking the signal or because of enemy jamming on the same radio frequencies.

To home in on targets, Auterion’s software relies solely on the visual information available from the Shrike drone’s main onboard camera. That means the Shrike drones can track and strike moving targets without any reliance on GPS—a crucial advantage on modern battlefields, where GPS jamming has also become common.

That could further enhance the success rate of remotely piloted Shrike drones that have already struck many vehicle-size targets since Russia launched the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, including armored tanks, electronic warfare systems, artillery guns, and rocket launchers. Shrike drones have reportedly taken down two Russian Mi-28 helicopters, each worth as much as $19 million, according to the Kyiv Independent.

Cost-effective AI for battlefield drones

Until now, the Ukrainian military has mainly relied on human operators to manually guide drones toward their targets, with the exception of mid- or long-range strike drones such as the $5,000 AI-powered “Hornet” drones developed by the California-based company Perennial Autonomy, founded by former Google CEO Eric Schmidt. Those drones often fly far beyond the frontlines to target Russian oil refineries and energy infrastructure, factories and warehouses, or even ships in the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea.

But Auterion focused on creating AI-powered capabilities for the cheaper, shorter-range FPV drones that have become the most common weapons responsible for killing or wounding soldiers on the frontlines in Ukraine. The company developed a tightly integrated flight control system and terminal guidance system optimized to run on a Western-made Arm system-on-a-chip costing just $18.

“What we are doing is replacing the existing flight controller—which has no computer, no AI—with avionics that has a microprocessor unit, has AI on board, and can track into the target fully autonomously,” Meier told Ars.

Each of SkyFall’s Shrike drones equipped with such capability costs about $2,000, compared to the $400 Ukrainian drones that rely only on manual piloting, Meier wrote in a blog post.

By comparison, he described Western militaries as still purchasing “precision munitions at six or seven figures per shot (30–60 times this price), drones procured in batches of dozens, priced like exquisite aircraft, delivered on timelines measured in years.”

The 50,000 Shrike drones equipped with Auterion’s strike kit were funded by a $100 million contract backed by an officially unnamed European country. Reuters reported that Germany is the country funding the order, and Meier also disclosed that Auterion’s team based in Munich, Germany, is fulfilling the order.

This is the largest delivery order to date for Auterion. But the company also previously committed to delivering 33,000 drone strike kits to Ukraine in July 2025, with backing from a $50 million Pentagon contract.

Human control and drone swarms

The drone strike kits would also enable SkyFall’s Shrike drones to receive future software updates that could enable a single human operator to command an autonomous swarm of drones to attack targets.

Auterion did not provide a timeframe for when this might happen. But the company has already demonstrated such drone swarming capability during a live-fire combat exercise at a US military range at Camp Blanding in Florida. The demonstration involved a drone pilot commanding three autonomous strike drones to take out three separate targets.

Such swarm capability provided by Auterion’s Nemyx system means that drones can autonomously work together to prioritize higher-value targets and adjust on the fly as targets are destroyed, so multiple drones aren’t wasted on the same target, Meier explained. That can all happen without any human input after the operator first directs the drone swarm toward a given objective.

“It basically means that you can point one of our swarms at an objective, and you can either decide to point all the munitions at a single target point, or you can actually spread them out from the get-go, and they will reprioritize,” Meier told Ars. “If you kick the swarm into strike mode, the whole thing strikes. If you let it abort, the whole thing aborts.”

The autonomous drone capabilities provided by Auterion’s strike kits also simplify the piloting skill required of human operators—regardless of whether they are piloting a single drone or commanding a swarm. That could help Ukraine’s military deploy more drones using a limited number of drone operators, and could prove even more invaluable for the United States or other countries that don’t yet have large numbers of trained drone operators.

“We found that we can train people within—I’m not kidding—60 seconds to operate this drone and even to operate the swarm, because you just move up and down to steer them in the right direction towards the target,” Meier said. “And when you are close enough to acquire the target, you just select it on the screen.”

The prospect of deploying fully autonomous drones on the battlefield may seem to be creeping closer. But Meier emphasized that Auterion believes in keeping a human in the target selection process.

“I am not sure if our adversaries eventually will allow us that, because they might enter into a way of warfare where we have to send autonomous systems against autonomous systems and let them make split-second decisions,” Meier said. “But until we are at that point, we as a company, and I personally believe, it’s really good if a human operator makes a life-or-death decision.”

Ukraine’s battlefield innovation system

Having visited Ukraine eight times to talk with the country’s top political and military leaders while working alongside Ukrainian drone manufacturers, Meier praised Ukraine for developing a system that enables a rapid cycle of innovation and improvement informed by battlefield experience.

“The Ukrainian forces are relatively accepting of initial battlefield failure,” Meier told Ars. “A lot of the Ukrainian firms didn’t show up with a perfectly working product—they showed up with something that was better than nothing, and then iterated through a lot of failures towards a point where it works every single time.”

Ukraine has also created an effective system for evaluating how well new drones and other weapons perform on the battlefield in terms of hit rates and delivering results of military value, Meier said. That feeds back into the cycle of innovation and has enabled Ukrainian companies to take huge risks in developing drones, robots and other weapons, while learning from failures on how to harden their systems for modern battlefields.

By comparison, the US military’s strict schedule for selecting new drone technologies through the Pentagon’s Drone Dominance program means that companies cannot easily come back several weeks later with a greatly improved product if they fail to make the cut at each selection stage. But Meier described Auterion as being well positioned to bring some lessons learned from Ukrainian battlefields back to compete within the more regimented US system.

The US military will also need the equivalent of a common operating system for its command and control systems to work seamlessly with autonomous drones from many different manufacturers as it looks to eventually deploy thousands of drones, Meier said. He described Auterion’s long-term ambition as creating a software ecosystem that allows various software companies to develop applications for many types of drones from different companies—a vision that draws from his own experience in developing open source software and open hardware standards used in the drone industry.

“You need the autonomy to fold into your command system, which means you need the same operating system, and maybe you can afford to integrate two or three—like there are apps for iOS and Android and I think that’s OK,” Meier said. “But you can’t have 15.”

Jeremy Hsu is a reporter exploring a wide range of topics across deep tech and AI. He has previously written for New Scientist, Scientific American, IEEE Spectrum, Wired, Undark Magazine and MIT Tech Review, among many other publications, about topics such as deepfakes, data centers, drones, battery tech, robotics, and GPS jamming. He also has a Master of Arts in Journalism from NYU, and a bachelor's degree from University of Pennsylvania in History and Sociology of Science, with a minor in English.

blocks.html_en: Human control and drone swarms

sentences.en: Human control and drone swarms
sentences.zh: 人类控制和无人机群

blocks.html_en: The drone strike kits would also enable SkyFall’s Shrike drones to receive future software updates that could enable a single human operator to command an autonomous swarm of drones to attack targets.

sentences.en: The drone strike kits would also enable SkyFall’s Shrike drones to receive future software updates that could enable a single human operator to command an autonomous swarm of drones to attack targets.
sentences.zh: 无人机攻击套件还将使 SkyFall 的 Shrike 无人机能够接收未来的软件更新，从而使单个操作员能够指挥一群自主无人机攻击目标。

blocks.html_en: Auterion did not provide a timeframe for when this might happen. But the company has already demonstrated such drone swarming capability during a live-fire combat exercise at a US military range at Camp Blanding in Florida. The demonstration involved a drone pilot commanding three autonomous strike drones to take out three separate targets.

sentences.en: Auterion did not provide a timeframe for when this might happen.
sentences.zh: Auterion 没有提供何时发生这种情况的时间表。

sentences.en: But the company has already demonstrated such drone swarming capability during a live-fire combat exercise at a US military range at Camp Blanding in Florida.
sentences.zh: 但该公司已经在佛罗里达州布兰丁营美军靶场的一次实弹作战演习中展示了这种无人机集群能力。

sentences.en: The demonstration involved a drone pilot commanding three autonomous strike drones to take out three separate targets.
sentences.zh: 演示中，一名无人机飞行员指挥三架自主攻击无人机摧毁三个不同的目标。

blocks.html_en: Such swarm capability provided by Auterion’s Nemyx system means that drones can autonomously work together to prioritize higher-value targets and adjust on the fly as targets are destroyed, so multiple drones aren’t wasted on the same target, Meier explained. That can all happen without any human input after the operator first directs the drone swarm toward a given objective.

sentences.en: Such swarm capability provided by Auterion’s Nemyx system means that drones can autonomously work together to prioritize higher-value targets and adjust on the fly as targets are destroyed, so multiple drones aren’t wasted on the same target, Meier explained.
sentences.zh: Meier 解释说，Auterion 的 Nemyx 系统提供的这种群体能力意味着无人机可以自主地协同工作，优先考虑更高价值的目标，并在目标被摧毁时进行动态调整，因此不会在同一个目标上浪费多架无人机。

sentences.en: That can all happen without any human input after the operator first directs the drone swarm toward a given objective.
sentences.zh: 在操作员首先将无人机群引向给定目标后，这一切都可以在没有任何人工输入的情况下发生。

blocks.html_en: “It basically means that you can point one of our swarms at an objective, and you can either decide to point all the munitions at a single target point, or you can actually spread them out from the get-go, and they will reprioritize,” Meier told Ars. “If you kick the swarm into strike mode, the whole thing strikes. If you let it abort, the whole thing aborts.”

sentences.en: “It basically means that you can point one of our swarms at an objective, and you can either decide to point all the munitions at a single target point, or you can actually spread them out from the get-go, and they will reprioritize,” Meier told Ars.
sentences.zh: “这基本上意味着你可以将我们的一个集群瞄准一个目标，你可以决定将所有弹药瞄准一个目标点，或者你可以从一开始就将它们分散开来，然后它们会重新调整优先级，”迈尔告诉Ars。

sentences.en: “If you kick the swarm into strike mode, the whole thing strikes.
sentences.zh: “如果你将蜂群踢入攻击模式，整个群体就会发起攻击。

sentences.en: If you let it abort, the whole thing aborts.”
sentences.zh: 如果你让它中止，那么整个事情就会中止。”

blocks.html_en: The autonomous drone capabilities provided by Auterion’s strike kits also simplify the piloting skill required of human operators—regardless of whether they are piloting a single drone or commanding a swarm. That could help Ukraine’s military deploy more drones using a limited number of drone operators, and could prove even more invaluable for the United States or other countries that don’t yet have large numbers of trained drone operators.

sentences.en: The autonomous drone capabilities provided by Auterion’s strike kits also simplify the piloting skill required of human operators—regardless of whether they are piloting a single drone or commanding a swarm.
sentences.zh: Auterion 攻击套件提供的自主无人机功能还简化了人类操作员所需的驾驶技能，无论他们是驾驶单架无人机还是指挥无人机群。

sentences.en: That could help Ukraine’s military deploy more drones using a limited number of drone operators, and could prove even more invaluable for the United States or other countries that don’t yet have large numbers of trained drone operators.
sentences.zh: 这可以帮助乌克兰军方使用有限数量的无人机操作员部署更多无人机，并且对于美国或其他尚未拥有大量训练有素的无人机操作员的国家来说可能更加无价。

blocks.html_en: “We found that we can train people within—I’m not kidding—60 seconds to operate this drone and even to operate the swarm, because you just move up and down to steer them in the right direction towards the target,” Meier said. “And when you are close enough to acquire the target, you just select it on the screen.”

sentences.en: “We found that we can train people within—I’m not kidding—60 seconds to operate this drone and even to operate the swarm, because you just move up and down to steer them in the right direction towards the target,” Meier said.
sentences.zh: “我们发现我们可以在 60 秒内（我不是开玩笑）训练人们操作这架无人机，甚至操作蜂群，因为你只需上下移动即可引导他们朝正确的方向飞向目标，”迈尔说。

sentences.en: “And when you are close enough to acquire the target, you just select it on the screen.”
sentences.zh: “当你足够接近目标时，你只需在屏幕上选择它即可。”

blocks.html_en: The prospect of deploying fully autonomous drones on the battlefield may seem to be creeping closer. But Meier emphasized that Auterion believes in keeping a human in the target selection process.

sentences.en: The prospect of deploying fully autonomous drones on the battlefield may seem to be creeping closer.
sentences.zh: 在战场上部署全自动无人机的前景似乎正在悄然逼近。

sentences.en: But Meier emphasized that Auterion believes in keeping a human in the target selection process.
sentences.zh: 但迈尔强调，Auterion 相信应该让人类参与目标选择过程。

blocks.html_en: “I am not sure if our adversaries eventually will allow us that, because they might enter into a way of warfare where we have to send autonomous systems against autonomous systems and let them make split-second decisions,” Meier said. “But until we are at that point, we as a company, and I personally believe, it’s really good if a human operator makes a life-or-death decision.”

sentences.en: “I am not sure if our adversaries eventually will allow us that, because they might enter into a way of warfare where we have to send autonomous systems against autonomous systems and let them make split-second decisions,” Meier said.
sentences.zh: 迈尔说：“我不确定我们的对手最终是否会允许我们这样做，因为他们可能会进入一种战争方式，我们必须派遣自主系统对抗自主系统，并让他们做出瞬间决定。”

sentences.en: “But until we are at that point, we as a company, and I personally believe, it’s really good if a human operator makes a life-or-death decision.”
sentences.zh: “但在那之前，我们作为一家公司，我个人认为，如果人类操作员做出生死攸关的决定，那真的很好。”

blocks.html_en: Ukraine’s battlefield innovation system

sentences.en: Ukraine’s battlefield innovation system
sentences.zh: 乌克兰战场创新系统

blocks.html_en: Having visited Ukraine eight times to talk with the country’s top political and military leaders while working alongside Ukrainian drone manufacturers, Meier praised Ukraine for developing a system that enables a rapid cycle of innovation and improvement informed by battlefield experience.

sentences.en: Having visited Ukraine eight times to talk with the country’s top political and military leaders while working alongside Ukrainian drone manufacturers, Meier praised Ukraine for developing a system that enables a rapid cycle of innovation and improvement informed by battlefield experience.
sentences.zh: 迈尔曾八次访问乌克兰，与该国最高政治和军事领导人交谈，同时与乌克兰无人机制造商合作，他赞扬乌克兰开发了一种系统，该系统能够根据战场经验实现快速创新和改进循环。

blocks.html_en: “The Ukrainian forces are relatively accepting of initial battlefield failure,” Meier told Ars. “A lot of the Ukrainian firms didn’t show up with a perfectly working product—they showed up with something that was better than nothing, and then iterated through a lot of failures towards a point where it works every single time.”

sentences.en: “The Ukrainian forces are relatively accepting of initial battlefield failure,” Meier told Ars.
sentences.zh: “乌克兰军队相对接受最初的战场失败，”迈尔告诉 Ars。

sentences.en: “A lot of the Ukrainian firms didn’t show up with a perfectly working product—they showed up with something that was better than nothing, and then iterated through a lot of failures towards a point where it works every single time.”
sentences.zh: “许多乌克兰公司并没有推出完美运行的产品——他们推出的产品总比没有好，然后经过多次失败，最终达到每次都能运行的程度。”

blocks.html_en: Ukraine has also created an effective system for evaluating how well new drones and other weapons perform on the battlefield in terms of hit rates and delivering results of military value, Meier said. That feeds back into the cycle of innovation and has enabled Ukrainian companies to take huge risks in developing drones, robots and other weapons, while learning from failures on how to harden their systems for modern battlefields.

sentences.en: Ukraine has also created an effective system for evaluating how well new drones and other weapons perform on the battlefield in terms of hit rates and delivering results of military value, Meier said.
sentences.zh: 迈尔说，乌克兰还创建了一个有效的系统，用于评估新型无人机和其他武器在战场上的命中率和军事价值成果。

sentences.en: That feeds back into the cycle of innovation and has enabled Ukrainian companies to take huge risks in developing drones, robots and other weapons, while learning from failures on how to harden their systems for modern battlefields.
sentences.zh: 这反馈到创新循环中，使乌克兰公司能够冒着巨大风险开发无人机、机器人和其他武器，同时从失败中学习如何强化现代战场的系统。

blocks.html_en: By comparison, the US military’s strict schedule for selecting new drone technologies through the Pentagon’s Drone Dominance program means that companies cannot easily come back several weeks later with a greatly improved product if they fail to make the cut at each selection stage. But Meier described Auterion as being well positioned to bring some lessons learned from Ukrainian battlefields back to compete within the more regimented US system.

sentences.en: But Meier described Auterion as being well positioned to bring some lessons learned from Ukrainian battlefields back to compete within the more regimented US system.
sentences.zh: 但迈耶表示，奥特里恩处于有利地位，可以将从乌克兰战场上吸取的一些经验教训带回美国，以便在更加严格的美国体系中竞争。

blocks.html_en: The US military will also need the equivalent of a common operating system for its command and control systems to work seamlessly with autonomous drones from many different manufacturers as it looks to eventually deploy thousands of drones, Meier said. He described Auterion’s long-term ambition as creating a software ecosystem that allows various software companies to develop applications for many types of drones from different companies—a vision that draws from his own experience in developing open source software and open hardware standards used in the drone industry.

sentences.zh: 迈尔说，美国军方还需要一个相当于通用操作系统的命令和控制系统，以便与许多不同制造商的自主无人机无缝协作，因为它希望最终部署数千架无人机。

sentences.en: He described Auterion’s long-term ambition as creating a software ecosystem that allows various software companies to develop applications for many types of drones from different companies—a vision that draws from his own experience in developing open source software and open hardware standards used in the drone industry.

content_html_zh:
蜂拥而至的时间到了

价值 1 亿美元的交易为 50,000 架乌克兰无人机提供了美国开发的人工智能功能。

配备 Auterion 的 Nemyx 集群自主系统的无人机在测试演示期间撞上了自行火炮。 图片来源：Lorenz Meier |奥特里翁

乌克兰无人机操作员使用价值 400 美元、携带爆炸物的 Shrike 无人机摧毁了许多地面的俄罗斯装甲车，甚至空中的军用直升机。 现在，数以千计的此类无人机正在升级，配备能够自动跟踪和追踪移动目标的人工智能系统。

7 月中旬，乌克兰军方开始接收由乌克兰公司 SkyFall 制造的 Shrike 无人机，配备由美国公司 Auterion 开发的人工智能驱动的自主硬件和软件。 两家公司计划在未来几个月内交付 50,000 架配备 Auterion Skynode S 攻击套件的无人机。

Auterion 联合创始人兼首席执行官洛伦茨·梅尔 (Lorenz Meier) 告诉 Ars，这使得人类操作员能够手动驾驶 Shrike 第一人称视角 (FPV) 无人机进入战场区域，指定半英里外的目标，然后“拨动开关将其转为即发即忘终端制导模式”。

迈尔解释说，只要操作员与无人机有无线电信号连接，他们就可以中止攻击或选择不同的目标。 但无人机仍然可以在没有任何人工指导的情况下自动跟踪并飞入目标，即使由于建筑物或地形阻挡信号或由于敌人干扰相同的无线电频率而失去与操作员的连接。

为了锁定目标，Auterion 的软件仅依赖于 Shrike 无人机主机载摄像头提供的视觉信息。 这意味着伯劳无人机可以在不依赖 GPS 的情况下跟踪和打击移动目标，这在 GPS 干扰也很常见的现代战场上是一个至关重要的优势。

这可能会进一步提高遥控伯劳无人机的成功率，自俄罗斯2022年对乌克兰发动全面入侵以来，伯劳无人机已经击中了许多车辆大小的目标，包括装甲坦克、电子战系统、火炮和火箭发射器。 据《基辅独立报》报道，伯劳无人机据称击落了两架俄罗斯 Mi-28 直升机，每架价值高达 1900 万美元。

适用于战场无人机的经济高效的人工智能

到目前为止，乌克兰军方主要依靠人类操作员手动引导无人机飞向目标，但中远程攻击无人机除外，例如谷歌前首席执行官埃里克·施密特创立的加州公司 Perennial Autonomy 开发的价值 5,000 美元的人工智能“大黄蜂”无人机。 这些无人机经常飞越前线，瞄准俄罗斯炼油厂和能源基础设施、工厂和仓库，甚至亚速海和黑海的船只。

但 Auterion 专注于为更便宜、航程较短的 FPV 无人机创造人工智能驱动的功能，这些无人机已成为乌克兰前线造成士兵伤亡的最常见武器。 该公司开发了一种紧密集成的飞行控制系统和终端制导系统，经过优化，可在西方制造的 Arm 片上系统上运行，成本仅为 18 美元。

“我们正在做的事情是用带有微处理器单元、机载人工智能并且可以完全自主跟踪目标的航空电子设备取代现有的飞行控制器（没有计算机，没有人工智能），”迈尔告诉 Ars。

迈耶在博客文章中写道，每架配备这种功能的 SkyFall 伯劳无人机的成本约为 2,000 美元，而乌克兰仅依靠手动驾驶的无人机售价为 400 美元。

相比之下，他形容西方军队仍在购买“每发六到七位数的精确弹药（这个价格的30到60倍），成批采购数十架无人机，价格像精致的飞机一样，交付时间以年为单位。”

配备 Auterion 攻击套件的 50,000 架 Shrike 无人机由一个官方未透露名称的欧洲国家支持的 1 亿美元合同提供资金。 路透社报道称，德国是该订单的资助国，Meier 还透露，位于德国慕尼黑的 Auterion 团队正在履行该订单。

这是 Auterion 迄今为止最大的交货订单。 但该公司此前还承诺在五角大楼价值 5000 万美元的合同的支持下，于 2025 年 7 月向乌克兰交付 33,000 个无人机攻击套件。

人类控制和无人机群

无人机攻击套件还将使 SkyFall 的 Shrike 无人机能够接收未来的软件更新，从而使单个操作员能够指挥一群自主无人机攻击目标。

Auterion 没有提供何时发生这种情况的时间表。 但该公司已经在佛罗里达州布兰丁营美军靶场的一次实弹作战演习中展示了这种无人机集群能力。 演示中，一名无人机飞行员指挥三架自主攻击无人机摧毁三个不同的目标。

Meier 解释说，Auterion 的 Nemyx 系统提供的这种群体能力意味着无人机可以自主地协同工作，优先考虑更高价值的目标，并在目标被摧毁时进行动态调整，因此不会在同一个目标上浪费多架无人机。 在操作员首先将无人机群引向给定目标后，这一切都可以在没有任何人工输入的情况下发生。

“这基本上意味着你可以将我们的一个集群瞄准一个目标，你可以决定将所有弹药瞄准一个目标点，或者你可以从一开始就将它们分散开来，然后它们会重新调整优先级，”迈尔告诉Ars。 “如果你将蜂群踢入攻击模式，整个群体就会发起攻击。 如果你让它中止，那么整个事情就会中止。”

Auterion 攻击套件提供的自主无人机功能还简化了人类操作员所需的驾驶技能，无论他们是驾驶单架无人机还是指挥无人机群。 这可以帮助乌克兰军方使用有限数量的无人机操作员部署更多无人机，并且对于美国或其他尚未拥有大量训练有素的无人机操作员的国家来说可能更加无价。

“我们发现我们可以在 60 秒内（我不是开玩笑）训练人们操作这架无人机，甚至操作蜂群，因为你只需上下移动即可引导他们朝正确的方向飞向目标，”迈尔说。 “当你足够接近目标时，你只需在屏幕上选择它即可。”

在战场上部署全自动无人机的前景似乎正在悄然逼近。 但迈尔强调，Auterion 相信应该让人类参与目标选择过程。

迈尔说：“我不确定我们的对手最终是否会允许我们这样做，因为他们可能会进入一种战争方式，我们必须派遣自主系统对抗自主系统，并让他们做出瞬间决定。” “但在那之前，我们作为一家公司，我个人认为，如果人类操作员做出生死攸关的决定，那真的很好。”

乌克兰战场创新系统

迈尔曾八次访问乌克兰，与该国最高政治和军事领导人交谈，同时与乌克兰无人机制造商合作，他赞扬乌克兰开发了一种系统，该系统能够根据战场经验实现快速创新和改进循环。

“乌克兰军队相对接受最初的战场失败，”迈尔告诉 Ars。 “许多乌克兰公司并没有推出完美运行的产品——他们推出的产品总比没有好，然后经过多次失败，最终达到每次都能运行的程度。”

迈尔说，乌克兰还创建了一个有效的系统，用于评估新型无人机和其他武器在战场上的命中率和军事价值成果。 这反馈到创新循环中，使乌克兰公司能够冒着巨大风险开发无人机、机器人和其他武器，同时从失败中学习如何强化现代战场的系统。

相比之下，美国军方通过五角大楼的无人机主导计划选择新无人机技术的严格时间表意味着，如果公司在每个选择阶段都未能通过，那么几周后就无法轻易带着大幅改进的产品回来。 但迈耶表示，奥特里恩处于有利地位，可以将从乌克兰战场上吸取的一些经验教训带回美国，以便在更加严格的美国体系中竞争。

迈尔说，美国军方还需要一个相当于通用操作系统的命令和控制系统，以便与许多不同制造商的自主无人机无缝协作，因为它希望最终部署数千架无人机。 他将 Auterion 的长期目标描述为创建一个软件生态系统，允许各种软件公司为不同公司的多种类型无人机开发应用程序，这一愿景源自他自己开发无人机行业使用的开源软件和开放硬件标准的经验。

“你需要自主权来融入你的命令系统，这意味着你需要相同的操作系统，也许你有能力集成两个或三个——就像有适用于 iOS 和 Android 的应用程序，我认为这没关系，”梅尔说。 “但你不能有15个。”
